questions.question: Who founded the Chola empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayalaya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chola Empire** was one of the** longest-ruling dynasties** in southern India, which existed from the **3rd century BCE** to the **13th century CE.**
 
• The **Chola dynasty** was known for its **maritime trade, art, literature, and architecture.**
 
• **Vijayalaya Chola** was the founder of the **Chola Empire **in **848 CE.**
 
• Vijayalaya Chola was a **Tamil ruler. **
 
• He conquered the regions of **Tanjore, Trichy, and parts of Pudukkottai and Tiruchirappalli,** which formed the nucleus of the Chola Empire.
 
• The Chola Empire reached its zenith under the reign of **Rajendra Chola I, **who conquered territories up to the Ganges in the north and the Malay Peninsula in the south.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dantidurga** was the founder of the** Rashtrakuta Empire **in the Deccan region.

 
 
• It existed from the **6th to the 10th **century CE.
 
 
 
• **Singhavishnu **was a ruler of the **Pallava dynasty.**
 
 
• It existed in the southern part of India from the **3rd to the 9th** century CE. 
 
 
 
• **Upendrarai** is not a known historical figure or ruler in Indian history.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy (2007) of the Government of India?

options.text: To maximise the focus on rehabilitation without really caring for resettlement
To integrate rehabilitation concerns into the development planning and implementation process
To minimise displacement and to promote, as far as possible, non-displacing or least-displacing alternatives
To provide a better standard of living, making concerted efforts for providing sustainable income to the affected families

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** To maximise the focus on rehabilitation without really caring for resettlement.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy (2007)** of the **Government of India** aims to provide better **living standards and sustainable income **to affected families.
 
• Another objective is to **integrate rehabilitation concerns** into the development planning and implementation process.
 
• The policy also aims to minimize displacement and promote **non-displacing or least-displacing alternatives.**
 
• However, the policy** does not** prioritize rehabilitation over resettlement.
 
• **Resettlement **is an important aspect of the policy, as it aims to provide affected families with a new place to live and sources of income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy **aims** to accomplish the following:

 
 
• **better living conditions** for affected families through coordinated efforts to provide sustainable income;
 
• integration of **rehabilitation **concerns into the development planning and implementation process; and,
 
• in cases where displacement is due to **land acquisition, **facilitation of harmonious relationships between the requiring body and affected families through mutual cooperation.
 
• The policy also ensures that special care is taken to **protect the rights of the weaker sections **of society, particularly members of the **Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes**, and creates obligations on the State for their treatment with concern and sensitivity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Earth's magnetic field?

options.text: To provide an energy source for life on Earth
To shield the Earth from solar wind and cosmic radiation
To cause the tides in the ocean

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To shield the Earth from solar wind and cosmic radiation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The purpose of the** Earth's magnetic field** is to shield the planet from **solar wind** and **cosmic radiation.**
 
• This is important because these particles can be harmful to **life on Earth** and can cause damage to our atmosphere.
 
• The Earth's magnetic field is generated by the movement of** molten iron** in the planet's core.
 
• This creates a **magnetic field **that extends out into space and protects the planet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Earth's magnetic field **does not** provide energy for life on Earth.
 
• While the Earth's magnetic field may have **some impact on the climate,** its primary purpose is to protect the planet from solar wind and cosmic radiation.
 
• The **tides** are primarily caused by the **gravitational pull **of the moon and the sun.
 
• The **magnetic field** that emanates from** Earth's interior **and interacts with the** solar wind,a stream of charged particles** that comes from the Sun, is called the geomagnetic field, or Earth's magnetic field.

questions.question: Which mineral salt is dissolved in a major amount in ocean water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium chloride.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium chloride**, also known as **table salt**, is a mineral salt that is dissolved in major amounts in **ocean water.**
 
• It is estimated that the ocean contains about **35 grams** of salt per liter of water, and about** 85% **of that salt is sodium chloride.
 
• **Calcium chloride and calcium sulfate** are also present in ocean water but in much **smaller amounts **compared to sodium chloride.
 
• Calcium carbonate is a mineral that is found in the** shells and skeletons** of many marine organisms, but it is** not dissolved **in ocean water as much as sodium chloride.
 
• The high concentration of sodium chloride in ocean water is one of the reasons why it is **not safe to drink** without proper treatment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium chloride** is a salt that is commonly used as a **de-icing agent** on roads and sidewalks, as well as in **food production and medical applications.**
 
• **Calcium sulphate**, also known as** gypsum**, is a mineral that is used in **construction, agriculture, and as a food additive.**
 
• **Calcium carbonate** is used in a variety of industries, including **construction, paper production, and as a dietary supplement.**
 
• It is important to note that while sodium chloride is the most **abundant mineral salt in ocean water,** there are also many other dissolved substances that contribute to the overall composition of seawater.

questions.question: X and Y are working as managers in a restaurant but they receive unequal pay for the same work. Which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy provides for equal pay for equal work?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 39.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy** provides for **equal pay for equal work.**
 
• **Article 39 **states that the State shall direct its policy towards **securing**, among other things, that there is **equal pay for equal work** for both men and women.
 
• This provision is aimed at **eliminating discrimination** in wages on the basis of** gender**, and ensuring that workers are paid fairly for the work they do.
 
• The Constitution of India recognizes the importance of ensuring **social and economic justice** for all, and the provision for equal pay for equal work is in line with this objective.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 38 **deals with the State's duty to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order in which** justice, social, economic and political,** shall inform all the institutions of national life.
 
• **Article 41** deals with the **right to work, education, and public assistance** in certain cases. 
 
• **Article 40** deals with the State's duty to organize **village panchayats** and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of National Highways in India?

options.text: Connect state capitals and major cities
Construction of border roads in high altitude areas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Construction of border roads in high-altitude areas.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Highways** in India are meant for **inter-state transport **and connect **state capitals** and major cities.
 
• They are maintained by the** Central Government **and are a crucial part of** India's transportation network.**
 
• **Border roads** in high-altitude areas are constructed by the **Border Roads Organisation (BRO)**, which is a separate entity from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
 
• The BRO constructs and maintains roads in difficult terrain and border areas to ensure** connectivity and strategic mobility** for the Indian Armed Forces.
 
• National Highways are identified by their unique numbers, which range from **1 to 373 **and cover a total length of over** 135,000 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Ministry of Road Transport and Highways** is the owner of India's network of trunk roads, known as the **national highways.**
 
• At 4,112 km (2,555 mi),** National Highway 44** is currently the longest National Highway in India.
 
• Major national highways in India were first four-laned under the** National Highway Development Project (NHDP).**
 
• India has about** 35,000 km** of **four-lane national highways** as of **March 2022.**

questions.question: The Government Budget is a statement of estimates of the government receipts and government expenditure for the coming financial year. The financial year for India is the period from _____to______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April 1 to March 31.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **financial year **for India is the period from **April 1 to March 31.**
 
• This means that the **government budget **estimates for the financial year are prepared based on the **expected receipts and expenditure** during this period.
 
• The government receipts include revenue from **taxes, non-tax sources, and borrowings**, while the government expenditure includes both **revenue and capital expenditure** on various sectors such as **defense, education, healthcare, infrastructure**, etc.
 
• The budget is an important tool for **fiscal management and policy-making**, as it reflects the government's priorities and goals for the economy and society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The financial year for India was earlier from **May 1 to April 30,** but it was changed to April 1 to March 31 in 1867.
 
• The government presents the budget in the Parliament in the form of two documents: the** Union Budget**, which includes the estimates for the central government, and the** State Budgets**, which include the estimates for the state governments.
 
• The budget also includes various measures to promote **economic growth, reduce fiscal deficits, and address social and welfare issues.**
 
• The government uses various fiscal instruments such as** taxes, subsidies, and transfers** to achieve its budgetary objectives.
 
• The budget is subject to approval by the **Parliament** and may be revised during the year if there are significant changes in the economic and financial situation.

questions.question: Which part of a cell converts nutrients into energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria** is the part of the cell that converts **nutrients into energy** in the form of** ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate).** 
 
• It is also known as the** powerhouse** of the cell.
 
• Mitochondria have their **own DNA **and can **reproduce themselves** within the cell. 
 
• It plays a crucial role in **cellular respiration**, which is the process of **converting glucose** and oxygen into ATP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell membrane**: It is the outermost part of the cell that controls the entry and exit of substances in and out of the cell.

 A semipermeable lipid bilayer forms the cell membrane.

 **Lysosomes: **These are organelles that contain enzymes to break down waste products and cellular debris.
 
• ​Digestive enzymes are found in lysosomes, which are membrane-bound cell organelles.

 **Chromosomes:** They are structures in the nucleus that contain genetic information in the form of DNA.

 Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and a protein molecule make up each chromosome.

 DNA contains the precise instructions that differentiate each type of living thing from one another and is passed from parents to children.

questions.question: What is the monomer unit of glycogen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glucose.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **monomer unit **of glycogen is** glucose.**
 
• **Glycogen** is a **complex carbohydrate** that is formed by the **polymerization of glucose** molecules.
 
• **Glucose** is a **simple sugar** that is the **primary source of energy** for the body.
 
• It is the **main free sugar** present in **higher animals' blood** and can be found in fruits and honey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fructose** is another simple sugar that is found in** fruits and honey.**

 
 
• Other plant foods like** honey, sugar beets, sugar cane, and vegetables** also naturally contain it.
 
• The** sweetest naturally **occurring carbohydrate is **fructose**. 
 
 
 
• **Galactose** is a simple sugar that is found in **milk and dairy products.**
 
 
• Usually, it is found in nature in** mixtures** with other sugars, like lactose (milk sugar).
 
 
 
• **Mannose** is a **simple sugar** that is found in some plants.
 
 
• It is used in the production of **glycoproteins and glycolipids**.

questions.question: Which of these statements is INCORRECT about Human Development Index?

options.text: The level of education is represented in the HDI
It uses the per capita GDP of a country on purchasing power parity terms to represent the income component.
Birth rate and death rate important components of the HDI
Life expectancy at birth is one of the components of the HDI.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Birth rate and death rate important components of the HDI.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a measure of **human development **that takes into account three dimensions: **health, education, and income.**
 
• The level of education is one of the components of the HDI, along with the **years of schooling **and the expected years of schooling.
 
• The income component of the HDI is represented by the **per capita GDP **of a country on **purchasing power parity terms**, which takes into account the differences in the cost of living between countries.
 
• **Life expectancy **at birth is another component of the HDI, as it reflects the** overall health **and well-being of a population.
 
• Birth rate and death rate are **not components** of the HDI, as they are considered to be** demographic indicators** rather than measures of human development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The HDI was developed by the** United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) **in **1990** as a way to measure progress in human development across countries.
 
• The HDI ranges from **0 to 1**, with higher values indicating **higher levels of human development.**
 
• The HDI is updated annually and is widely used by **policymakers, researchers, and advocates** to track progress in human development and identify areas for improvement.
 
• Other measures of human development include the** Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI),** which takes into account a broader range of dimensions of poverty beyond income, and the **Gender Development Index (GDI)**, which measures gender gaps in education, health, and income.

questions.question: Which of the following noble ideals is mentioned in the preamble of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Liberty of expression, civil, political, worship and belief
Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
Liberty of belief, fiscal, personal, faith and worship
Liberty of opportunity, economic, social, faith and expression

questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **The preamble** mentions **"Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship"** as one of the noble ideals mentioned in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Indian Constitution's preamble outlines the** fundamental principles** and** values** that guide the country and its people.
 
• It begins with the words** "We, the people of India,"** emphasizing the democratic nature of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian Constitution** is the ultimate law of the land based on the idea put forth by **M.N. Roy.**
 
• It is the document that lays out the framework that defines the **fundamental political code, structure, procedures, powers, and duties** of government institutions.
 
• It also lays out **fundamental rights, directive principles**, and the **duties **of citizens.
 
• It's the world's **longest written national constitution.**
 
• On** November 26, 1949,** the Indian Constituent Assembly adopted it, and on **January 26, 1950**, it came into force. 
 
• The **Government of India Act 1935 **was superseded by the constitution in **1935**, transforming the Dominion of India into the **Republic of India.**

questions.question: In which language was the work of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 'Gift to Monotheists' originally written?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Persian.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy'**s work, **'Gift to Monotheists',** was originally written in **Persian.**
 
• Persian was a widely used language in India during the** Mughal era** and was the** language of the court.**
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a prominent **social reformer **and **scholar **who played a key role in the **Indian Renaissance.**
 
• The work, 'Gift to Monotheists', was a critique of **polytheism **and an argument for the** superiority of monotheistic religions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arabic** is a language primarily associated with** Islam **and is widely used in **religious texts and rituals.**

 
 
• The majority of speakers of the **Semitic language** Arabic are found in the **Arab world.**
 
• It is named after the Arab people and first appeared in the** first century AD.**
 
 
 
• **Bengali** is the language of the Bengali people of** eastern India** and **Bangladesh** and has a rich literary tradition.
 
 
• It is the official language of **West Bengal, Tripura,** and the** Assamese Barak Valley.**
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit** is an ancient language of India and is associated with **Hinduism **and traditional Indian knowledge systems.
 
 
• Following the dispersal of its predecessor languages from the** northwest **during the late Bronze Age, it originated in **South Asia.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the best estimate of the total borrowings by the government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Deficit.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **A fiscal deficit **represents the difference between the **government's total expenditure** and its **total revenue**.
 
• It is a key indicator of the **government's borrowings** and reflects the extent to which it is relying on debt to fund its spending.
 
• **Primary deficit** is a narrower measure that **excludes interest payments** on past borrowings.
 
• It indicates the government's borrowing needs for **current spending** but does not capture the burden of past debt.
 
• **Revenue receipts **represent the government's income from** taxes, fees, and other sources.** 
 
• **Money supply** is a measure of the total amount of** money in circulation** in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue receipts **can be further classified into **tax revenue and non-tax revenue.**
 
• Tax revenue is the income from taxes such as **income tax, corporate tax, GST, etc.**
 
• Non-tax revenue is the income from other sources such as** dividends from public sector enterprises, interest receipts, etc.**
 
• **Money supply **can be measured in different ways, such as** M1, M2, and M3**.
 
• M1 includes currency in** circulation, demand deposits,** and other liquid assets.
 
• M2 includes **M1 plus savings deposits, time deposits,** and other less liquid assets.
 
• M3 includes **M2 plus large time deposits and institutional money market funds.**

questions.question: Which of the following states receives rainfall during the retreating monsoon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu** receives rainfall during the **retreating monsoon,** which is also known as the** northeast monsoon** or the **post-monsoon season**.
 
• The retreating monsoon refers to the** withdrawal of the southwest monsoon** from the Indian subcontinent, which usually occurs from** September to December.**
 
• **Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and Bihar **receive rainfall during the southwest monsoon season, which lasts from **June to September.**
 
• Tamil Nadu, on the other hand, experiences a** dry season** during the southwest monsoon and relies on the **retreating monsoon **for its rainfall.
 
• Tamil Nadu's agriculture, particularly its** rice and millet crops,** depends heavily on the retreating monsoon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is a central state of India that receives rainfall from the **southwest monsoon.**

 
 
• It is one of the largest producers of **soybeans, wheat, and pulses** in the country.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat** is a western state of India that receives rainfall from the** southwest monsoon.**
 
 
• It is known for its **cotton, groundnut, and oilseed **production.
 
 
 
• **Bihar** is an eastern state of India that receives rainfall from the **southwest monsoon**.
 
 
• It is one of the largest producers of** vegetables, fruits, and flowers** in the country.
